<pr_description>
Consider the following PR description:
Refactor `createWrapper` to generate wrapper function via string concatenation and `eval`

**Body:**

Currently, `createWrapper` takes a function `fn` and returns a new function that wraps `fn`. This creates a closure for every wrapped function, which can be avoided by generating the wrapper as a string of JavaScript code and then evaluating it.

Refactor `createWrapper` to accept a `name` string (the original function’s name) and an `options` object, and return a string that, when evaluated, produces the wrapper function. Update the call sites in `thenify` and `thenify.withCallback` to pass `fn.name` (the function’s name) to `createWrapper` and then use `eval()` on the returned string to obtain the wrapper.

In `createWrapper`, build the function body as a string that declares `var self = this`, `var len = arguments.length`, and includes the `multiArgs` default and `withCallback` logic directly in the generated code. Move the default for `multiArgs` (previously in `createCallback`) into the generated string: default to `true` unless `options.multiArgs` is explicitly provided.

In `thenify.withCallback`, set `options.multiArgs` to `true` if it is `undefined` before calling `createWrapper`, to preserve the previous default behavior (which was implicitly true because `createCallback` defaulted to `true`).

In `createCallback`, remove the `multiArgs === undefined` default assignment; it will now always be passed from the generated wrapper code.

Update the test file (`test/test.js`) to remove the two tests:
- “unicode function name” – tests a function with a name containing Unicode and special characters.
- “invalid function name” – tests a function with a name that contains characters invalid in a JavaScript identifier.

These names cannot be used in a `function` declaration inside the generated code, so they are no longer supported.

The result should be functionally identical for all valid function names, with no performance regression and the same behavior for `multiArgs` defaults.
</pr_description>

var Promise = require('any-promise')
var assert = require('assert')

module.exports = thenify

/**
 * Turn async functions into promises
 *
 * @param {Function} fn
 * @return {Function}
 * @api public
 */

function thenify(fn, options) {
  assert(typeof fn === 'function')
  return createWrapper(fn, options)
}

/**
 * Turn async functions into promises and backward compatible with callback
 *
 * @param {Function} fn
 * @return {Function}
 * @api public
 */

thenify.withCallback = function (fn, options) {
  assert(typeof fn === 'function')
  options = options || {}
  options.withCallback = true
  return createWrapper(fn, options)
}

function createCallback(resolve, reject, multiArgs) {
  // default to true
  if (multiArgs === undefined) multiArgs = true
  return function(err, value) {
    if (err) return reject(err)
    var length = arguments.length

    if (length <= 2 || !multiArgs) return resolve(value)

    if (Array.isArray(multiArgs)) {
      var values = {}
      for (var i = 1; i < length; i++) values[multiArgs[i - 1]] = arguments[i]
      return resolve(values)
    }

    var values = new Array(length - 1)
    for (var i = 1; i < length; ++i) values[i - 1] = arguments[i]
    resolve(values)
  }
}

function createWrapper(fn, options) {
  options = options || {}
  var name = fn.name;
  name = (name || '').replace(/\s|bound(?!$)/g, '')
  var newFn = function () {
    var self = this
    var len = arguments.length
    if (options.withCallback) {
      var lastType = typeof arguments[len - 1]
      if (lastType === 'function') return fn.apply(self, arguments)
    }
    var args = new Array(len + 1)
    for (var i = 0; i < len; ++i) args[i] = arguments[i]
    var lastIndex = i
    return new Promise(function (resolve, reject) {
      args[lastIndex] = createCallback(resolve, reject, options.multiArgs)
      fn.apply(self, args)
    })
  }
  Object.defineProperty(newFn, 'name', { value: name })
  return newFn
}
</output>

var thenify = require('..')

it('fn.name', function () {
  function someCrazyName() {}

  assert.equal('someCrazyName', thenify(someCrazyName).name)
  assert.equal('someCrazyName', thenify(someCrazyName).name)
  // In ES6 spec, functions can infer the name of an anonymous function from its syntactic position.
  var noname = function () {}
  var name = noname.name

  assert.equal(name, thenify(noname).name)
  assert.equal(name, thenify.withCallback(noname).name)
})

it('fn.name (bound function)', function () {
  function bound() {}
  assert.equal('bound', thenify(bound).name)
  assert.equal('bound', thenify.withCallback(bound).name)

  var noname = (function () {}).bind(this)
  assert.equal('', thenify(noname).name)
  assert.equal('', thenify.withCallback(noname).name)
})

it('fn(callback(err))', function () {
  function fn(cb) {
    setTimeout(function () {
      cb(new Error('boom'))
    }, 0)
  }

  return thenify(fn)().then(function () {
    throw new Error('bang')
  }).catch(function (err) {
    assert.equal(err.message, 'boom')
  })
})

it('fn(callback(null, value))', function () {
  function fn(cb) {
    cb(null, true)
  }

  return thenify(fn)().then(function (val) {
    assert.equal(val, true)
  })
})

it('fn(callback(null, values...))', function () {
  function fn(cb) {
    cb(null, 1, 2, 3)
  }

  return thenify(fn)().then(function (values) {
    assert.deepEqual(values, [1, 2, 3])
  })
})

  function fn(a, b, c, cb) {
